title: ARIA dialogs need an accessible name
summary: An element with role dialog or alertdialog has no accessible name. Label it with its visible heading using aria-labeledby.
problem: An element with role="dialog" or role="alertdialog" has no accessible name. When it opens, assistive technology can say a dialog appeared, but not what it is for.
whoItAffects: Screen reader users who land in a dialog hear nothing about its purpose, such as whether it is a sign-in form or a cookie notice. They may have to explore the content to work it out.
steps: Find the dialog element in the scan result.
If the dialog has a visible heading, give the heading an id and point to it with aria-labeledby on the dialog.
If there is no visible title, add a short aria-label that says what the dialog is for.
Keep the name short and specific, and do not include the word "dialog", since the role is announced already.

whyItMatters: This is a best practice, not a WCAG failure. A named dialog helps people confirm that they are in the right place, and it is a small change that is easy to carry into a reusable component.
howToCheck: Select the dialog in your browser's accessibility inspector and check that its Name matches the heading. A screen reader should announce the name when the dialog opens.
